lesson: A tool schema that syntactically accepts a training action is insufficient for a causal agent experiment. Every accepted action that can define an intervention boundary must have outcome-independent semantic observability: the runtime must either produce a verifiable persisted parameter update or reject the configuration before the scientific unit starts. Otherwise an agent can legitimately select a bounded action that numerically produces no detectable update, collapsing scientific non-adherence into support failure.
additional_engineering_lesson: Paid provider events must be persisted incrementally before executing a potentially failing tool. Keeping provider receipts only in memory until arm completion can lose exact cost/provenance accounting when a tool raises.
recommended_system_rule: Before authorizing a paid causal arm, audit the full accepted action surface for semantic boundary observability and use append-only per-provider-call receipts. Failures of semantic observability map to NO_EVIDENCE and cannot advance ProblemGate.
